content:
We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with 3 reactions for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

Let's parse: It's a tolyl (para methyl) phenyl sulfonamide attached to another phenyl with a trans-α,β-unsaturated amide linking to an aniline (c3ccccc3N). So overall: p-tolyl-sulfonyl-phenyl-CH=CH-CO-NH-aniline.

We need 3 steps retrosynthesis: likely disconnections:

1) Amide formation: break C(=O)-NH bond between the α,β-unsaturated carbonyl and the aniline. So precursor: trans-α,β-unsaturated acid (cinnamic acid derivative) attached to phenyl-sulfonyl phenyl, and aniline as nucleophile. So step1: coupling of aniline with α,β-unsaturated acid (cinnamic acid) to give amide.

2) Formation of the α,β-unsaturated acid via Doebner modification: from aromatic aldehyde (p-tolyl-sulfonyl phenyl aldehyde) + malonic acid -> trans-α,β-unsaturated acid (cinnamic acid derivative). So break C=C double bond formation, break C-C bond (malonic decarboxylation). So precursor: aldehyde (p-tolyl-sulfonyl phenyl aldehyde) and malonic acid (or maybe just malonic acid is a simple reagent, not a precursor). In retrosynthesis we can consider aldehyde as precursor.

3) Sulfonamide formation: break S-N bond between sulfonyl chloride and aniline? Actually sulfonamide attached to p-tolyl-sulfonyl group attached to phenyl. The sulfonamide is attached to the phenyl ring (the sulfonyl attached to phenyl, and the nitrogen attached to the phenyl ring? Wait structure: NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(... )cc2 attached to tolyl ring. So sulfonamide nitrogen attached to tolyl ring (p-tolyl) and sulfonyl attached to second phenyl. So sulfonamide formation could be from sulfonyl chloride (p-tolyl-sulfonyl chloride) reacting with aniline (the phenyl ring? Actually the nitrogen is attached to the tolyl ring, not aniline. The nitrogen is part of the tolyl ring? The SMILES: Cc1ccc(N S(=O)(=O) c2ccc(... )cc2)cc1. So the nitrogen is attached to the tolyl ring (as an aniline) and also to the sulfonyl group (sulfonamide). So the sulfonamide formation step: start from p-toluidine (aniline with methyl) and sulfonyl chloride (aryl sulfonyl chloride). So precursor: p-toluidine and aryl sulfonyl chloride (the second phenyl sulfonyl chloride). The aryl sulfonyl chloride is derived from the second phenyl (c2ccc(... )cc2) with sulfonyl chloride group.

Thus three steps:

Step A (last forward): sulfonamide formation: p-toluidine + aryl sulfonyl chloride -> target sulfonamide.

Step B: amide formation: aniline (c3ccccc3N) + trans-α,β-unsaturated acid (cinnamic acid derivative) -> amide (the part linking to aniline). But note the nitrogen in amide is the aniline nitrogen, not the sulfonamide nitrogen. So the amide formation uses aniline as nucleophile.

Step C: Doebner modification: aldehyde (aryl aldehyde) + malonic acid -> trans-α,β-unsaturated acid (cinnamic acid derivative). The aldehyde is the aryl sulfonyl phenyl aldehyde (c2ccc(C=O)cc2 attached to sulfonyl). So we need to generate that aldehyde from sulfonyl chloride? Actually the aldehyde is part of the aryl sulfonyl phenyl ring; we can get it via oxidation of the corresponding alcohol or via formylation. But we have only three steps total, so we need to incorporate aldehyde formation maybe as part of sulfonyl chloride precursor? Wait we already used sulfonyl chloride as a precursor for sulfonamide formation. That sulfonyl chloride is the aryl sulfonyl chloride (c2ccc(... )cc2 with sulfonyl chloride). That aryl sulfonyl chloride must have the aldehyde already present? The target sulfonyl phenyl has the aldehyde replaced by the α,β-unsaturated acid after Doebner. So the sulfonyl chloride precursor would be the same aryl ring but with sulfonyl chloride instead of sulfonyl attached to the tolyl? Actually the sulfonyl chloride is attached to the aryl ring (the second phenyl). The sulfonyl group is attached to the tolyl nitrogen, not to the second phenyl. Wait the sulfonyl group is S(=O)(=O) attached to the second phenyl (c2ccc(... )cc2). The nitrogen is attached to the sulfonyl group and to the tolyl ring. So the sulfonyl chloride precursor would be the same aryl sulfonyl chloride (Ar-SO2Cl) where Ar is the second phenyl with the α,β-unsaturated acid substituent? Actually after Doebner, the second phenyl has the α,β-unsaturated amide substituent. So the sulfonyl chloride precursor would have the same phenyl but with a sulfonyl chloride group instead of the sulfonyl attached to nitrogen? Wait the sulfonyl chloride is the electrophile for sulfonamide formation: Ar-SO2Cl reacts with p-toluidine to give Ar-SO2-NH-Ar'. In our target, the sulfonyl group is attached to the second phenyl (Ar) and the nitrogen attached to the tolyl ring. So the sulfonyl chloride precursor is the second phenyl sulfonyl chloride (Ar-SO2Cl). This Ar must already have the α,β-unsaturated amide substituent attached (the cinnamoyl amide). So we need to have that substituent present before sulfonamide formation. That means the Doebner step must be applied to the aryl sulfonyl chloride? But Doebner modifies an aldehyde to α,β-unsaturated acid, not sulfonyl chloride. So perhaps the order is: first Doebner on aldehyde (aryl aldehyde) to give α,β-unsaturated acid attached to aryl. Then convert that acid to amide with aniline (amide formation). Then convert the resulting aryl-sulfonyl amide? Wait the sulfonyl group is attached to the aryl, not to the amide. The sulfonyl group is attached to the aryl ring, independent of the amide side chain. So the sulfonyl chloride precursor would be the aryl ring bearing the α,β-unsaturated acid (cinnamic acid) and a sulfonyl chloride group (SO2Cl). Then after amide formation, we have aryl-sulfonyl amide? Actually the amide is attached to the α,β-unsaturated carbonyl, not to the sulfonyl. So the sulfonyl chloride is separate.

Thus three steps could be:

1) Sulfonamide formation: p-toluidine + aryl sulfonyl chloride (which already contains the α,β-unsaturated amide side chain) -> target.

2) Amide formation: aniline + α,β-unsaturated acid (cinnamic acid derivative) -> α,β-unsaturated amide (the side chain). This amide is attached to the aryl sulfonyl chloride? Wait the amide is attached to the aryl ring via the double bond: /C=C/C(=O)N-Ph. So the α,β-unsaturated acid is attached to the aryl ring at the para position (c2ccc(... )cc2). So the aryl sulfonyl chloride must have that side chain attached already. So step 2 must be applied to the aryl sulfonyl chloride? Actually the amide formation attaches the aniline to the carbonyl of the α,β-unsaturated acid, which is attached to the aryl ring. So the precursor for step 2 is the aryl sulfonyl chloride bearing the α,β-unsaturated acid (cinnamic acid). So we need to generate that acid via Doebner from aldehyde.

Thus step 3 (first retrosynthetic) is Doebner: aryl sulfonyl chloride bearing aldehyde (Ar-CHO) + malonic acid -> aryl sulfonyl chloride bearing α,β-unsaturated acid.

Thus overall three steps: (retro) 1) break sulfonamide S-N to give p-toluidine and aryl sulfonyl chloride with side chain. 2) break amide C-N to give aniline and aryl sulfonyl chloride α,β-unsaturated acid. 3) break α,β-unsaturated acid to aldehyde + malonic acid (or just aldehyde as precursor). So we need to propose route with SMILES for each intermediate.

Let's construct SMILES:

Target: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

Intermediate 1 (after breaking sulfonamide): p-toluidine (Cc1ccc(N)cc1) and aryl sulfonyl chloride with side chain: S(=O)(=O)Cl attached to phenyl bearing the side chain. SMILES for aryl sulfonyl chloride: S(=O)(=O)Cl attached to phenyl: ClS(=O)(=O)c1ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc2ccccc2N)cc1? Wait the sulfonyl chloride is attached to the phenyl (the second phenyl). So SMILES: ClS(=O)(=O)c1ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc2ccccc2N)cc1. That is the aryl sulfonyl chloride.

Intermediate 2 (after breaking amide): aniline (c1ccccc1N) and aryl sulfonyl chloride bearing α,β-unsaturated acid (cinnamic acid). So the acid SMILES: O=C(O)/C=C/c1ccc(ClS(=O)(=O)?) Wait the sulfonyl chloride is attached to phenyl, not to the acid. The acid is attached to phenyl at para position relative to sulfonyl chloride? In target, the sulfonyl group is attached to phenyl at position 1, and the side chain at para? Actually SMILES: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2 attached to S(=O)(=O). So the phenyl has the side chain at para to the sulfonyl? The SMILES shows c2ccc(... )cc2 attached directly to S(=O)(=O). So the side chain is attached to the phenyl at the position where the sulfonyl attaches? Wait the SMILES: NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2. So the sulfonyl attaches to the phenyl at the same carbon as the side chain? Actually the sulfonyl attaches to the phenyl via S attached to the phenyl carbon (aryl sulfone). The side chain is attached to the phenyl via a carbon (the same carbon? No, the side chain is attached to the phenyl via a carbon of the phenyl (the para position). The SMILES: c2ccc(/C=C/... )cc2 means the phenyl has a substituent /C=C/... at one position. The S(=O)(=O) attaches to the phenyl at the same carbon? The SMILES: S(=O)(=O)c2ccc(... )cc2 indicates the sulfonyl attaches to the phenyl at the carbon preceding the aromatic ring (i.e., the sulfonyl attached to the phenyl as a substituent). So the phenyl has two substituents: the sulfonyl attached to the nitrogen (forming sulfonamide) and the side chain attached at para position. So the aryl sulfonyl chloride precursor would have the sulfonyl chloride attached to the phenyl (ClS(=O)(=O)-Ph) and the side chain as aldehyde (or acid). So the SMILES for aryl sulfonyl chloride with aldehyde: ClS(=O)(=O)c1ccc(C=O)cc1 (para aldehyde). For acid: ClS(=O)(=O)c1ccc(C(=O)O)cc1.

Thus step 3: aldehyde precursor: ClS(=O)(=O)c1ccc(C=O)cc1 (aryl sulfonyl chloride aldehyde). Reaction with malonic acid (malonic acid SMILES: C(C(=O)O)C(=O)O) via Doebner to give aryl sulfonyl chloride cinnamic acid: ClS(=O)(=O)c1ccc(C=CC(=O)O)cc1 (trans). Actually product is α,β-unsaturated acid: C=CC(=O)O attached to phenyl.

Step 2: amide formation: aniline (c1ccccc1N) + aryl sulfonyl chloride cinnamic acid -> aryl sulfonyl chloride cinnamic amide (the side chain amide). SMILES: ClS(=O)(=O)c1ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc2ccccc2N)cc1.

Step 1: sulfonamide formation: p-toluidine (Cc1ccc(N)cc1) + aryl sulfonyl chloride cinnamic amide -> target.

Thus we have three steps.

Now we need template IDs for each reaction. We need to search for templates matching these transformations.

Step 1: sulfonamide formation: functional_groups_formed: sulfonamides, bonds_formed: S-N. Use search_template_catalog_by_criteria with functional_groups_formed ["sulfonamides"] maybe also bonds_formed? But we need template ID. Let's search for sulfonamide formation.
